word.shortDefinition: Draws a conclusion or starts a thought.

intro.title: Also doesn't mean 'also'
paragraphs: Also looks exactly like the English word, but it means 'so' or 'therefore'. Germans also use it the way English speakers say 'so…' or 'well…' to start a sentence. For 'also', German says auch.

keyTrap.title: The big trap: also is 'so'
keyTrap.explanation: When you mean 'too' or 'as well', you need auch.

correct.german: Es regnet, also bleiben wir zu Hause.
correct.literal: It's raining, so we stay at home.

commonMistakes.title: Word order after also
commonMistakes.explanation: When also starts the clause, the verb comes right after it.
commonMistakes.wrong: Es ist spät, also ich gehe.
commonMistakes.correct: Es ist spät, also gehe ich.

sampleSentences.german: Er hat keine Zeit, also kommt er nicht.
sampleSentences.english: He has no time, so he isn't coming.
So, what would you like to drink?

sampleSentences.german: Also gut, machen wir das so.
sampleSentences.english: All right then, let's do it that way.

memoryHook: Also = so. Auch = also. Swap them in your head.

quiz.prompt: Ich trinke Tee, und meine Frau trinkt ___ Tee. (too)
Der Laden ist zu, ___ gehen wir nach Hause. (so)

options: Es ist spät, also ich gehe.
Es ist spät, also gehe ich.
quiz.answer: Es ist spät, also gehe ich.
quiz.explanation: The verb comes right after also.

quiz.prompt: Ich bin ___ Lehrerin. (I'm a teacher too.)
